title: BitMix cost inspector: per-profile quant tradeoff calculator
content:
Purpose:
This is a working worksheet + recommendation draft for a 'BitMix' quant tradeoff inspector: a compact calculator to estimate cost, quality impact, and tail latency for different quantization strategies (per-layer mixed-precision, global INT8/FP8/4-bit, hybrid KV-cache use) across representative serving profiles. The goal is to make quick trade decisions for Dedicated and Hosted capacity recommendations and feed the Optimize product recommender.

Executive summary (working):
- For short-chat workloads (< 128 tokens) FP8 on attention-heavy models gives latency benefits at modest quality loss vs baseline FP16; INT8 usually wins cost for throughput-bound batch workloads.
- 4-bit (GPTQ-like) is only recommended in constrained-cost scenarios when prompt structure is stable and we've validated on eval prompts; per-layer 4-bit on embeddings/first/last layers often reduces quality degradation.
- Mixed-precision (KV-cache INT8 + attention FP8) seems promising for many production chat workloads; this doc outlines the calculator and heuristics for recommending it automatically.

Assumptions and input knobs (spreadsheet columns in the calculator):
- model_name (string): e.g. redwood-13b, open-30b
- seq_len_inference (int): typical response length (tokens)
- prompt_prefix_len (int): prefix tokens that are static/cached
- rps (float): requests per second steady-state
- batch_size_policy (string): 'latency-first' | 'throughput-first' | 'mixed'
- hw_profile (string): A100-80GB | H100-80GB | L4-mini (placeholder)
- quant_profile (string): global-int8 | global-fp8 | 4bit-gptq | mixed-bitmix (per-layer spec)
- cache_strategy (string): none | prefix-kv | full-kv
- quality_metric_pct_loss (float): estimated relative quality drop vs fp16 on eval set (user-provided or model-based estimate)

Calculator methodology (how numbers are derived):
1) Token-cost model: baseline per-token GPU-second from microbenchmarks (table included) scaled by batch size and hw. Multiply by cloud unit cost to compute $/1k tokens.
2) Latency model: per-request latency = infer-startup + (tokens_out * per-token-latency). Per-token latency depends on quant_profile and whether KV cache hits. We model tail (p95) as baseline*p95_multiplier (tunable).
3) Quality penalty: user-provided or a prediction model that infers expected eval-win rate degradation. For mixed profiles we compute weighted average by layer importance proxy.
4) Confidence ranges: Monte Carlo bootstrap with +/- 10-25% uncertainty on per-token latency and quality-loss to reflect dataset/model variability.

Sample spreadsheet rows (copy/paste friendly plain text table):
model_name,seq_len_inference,prompt_prefix_len,rps,batch_policy,hw_profile,quant_profile,cache_strategy,est_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd,est_p95_latency_ms,est_quality_loss_pct,notes
redwood-13b,64,32,15,latency-first,A100-80GB,global-int8,prefix-kv,0.42,78,3.5,good cost but slight deg on long-context
redwood-13b,64,32,15,latency-first,A100-80GB,global-fp8,prefix-kv,0.61,65,2.2,lower latency than int8 for this profile; higher cost
redwood-13b,64,32,15,latency-first,A100-80GB,mixed-bitmix,prefix-kv,0.47,60,1.8,mixed: attention fp8 + matmul/int8 yields best latency/quality balance
open-30b,128,80,5,throughput-first,H100-80GB,4bit-gptq,full-kv,0.33,210,7.6,4-bit has big quality hit on few-shot

Heuristics / Recommendation rules (draft):
- If est_quality_loss_pct > 5% => mark 'requires eval set signoff' before rollout.
- If rps < 2 and latency-first => prefer fp8 over int8 when p95 latency improves by >10% and quality_loss_pct delta <= 2%.
- If steady-state rps > 20 or batch_policy == throughput-first => prefer INT8 or 4-bit if quality loss <= 4% and operator accepts occasional regen failures.
- For models > 30B, require per-layer calibration simulation before recommending 4-bit.
- KV-cache: when prompt_prefix_len >= 40 and cache_strategy != none => prefer mixed-bitmix to quantize not-cached layers more aggressively.

Open design questions / unresolved knobs (notes to self):
- Need a simple per-layer importance heuristic. Current placeholder: layer_importance = position-based weight (first/last layers weight=1.4, mid layers=1.0). This is crude.
- How to account for compiler/kernel differences (A100 vs H100) beyond a single scalar multiplier? Should import actual microbenchmarks per kernel.
- How to represent hallucination risk vs numeric quality drop? We currently map both to a single quality_loss_pct, but downstream users want explicit hallucination probability.
- UX: expose a 'safe' suggestion and an 'aggressive' suggestion with validation T-tests to decide rollout.

Validation plan (experiments we need):
- Run quant-sim bench (see linked repo) for redwood-13b and open-30b across INT8, FP8, 4-bit per-layer combos; produce per-token latency tables. (Owner: Diego)
- Run eval harness on 2k prompt/eval set to measure quality_loss_pct and hallucination categories for each quant profile. (Owner: Priya)
- Small canary on Dedicated (one cluster) with synthetic traffic to validate p95 and p99 latencies. (Owner: Arjun)

Implementation notes for product recommender integration:
- Output format: CSV with columns above plus 'recommendation_type' (safe|aggressive|manual-review) and 'confidence_bucket' (low|medium|high).
- Store per-model calibration artifacts in bucket /optimize/quant-calibration/<model>/<date>/summary.json (TODO: coordinate with infra team).
- Add a 'why' field explaining rule trigger (e.g., 'p95-latency-reduction-12pct' or 'quality-loss>5pct').

Rollout proposal:
- Phase 0: internal team-only tool to produce reports and recommendations for 10 models.
- Phase 1: opt-in customers (Dedicated) where SE verifies recommendations during onboarding.
- Phase 2: automated in-console recommender with opt-out and pre-deploy eval job.

Quick TODO checklist (short):
- [ ] Wire microbenchmark table into spreadsheet backend.
- [ ] Replace crude layer_importance with attention-weight-derived importance from profiling.
- [ ] Add per-hardware kernel multipliers from release-engineering.
- [ ] Draft canary playbook for SRE (rollback thresholds, metrics to monitor).

Questions for reviewers:
- Which threshold for 'requires eval set signoff' is acceptable to Product and Trust & Safety? Proposed: 5% quality-loss or >2% hallucination rate.
- Any objections to naming the mixed-profile 'bitmix' to avoid collision with 'hybrid' in infra code?

Notes to self and rough references:
- See quant-sim PR for the microbench harness: linked_artifacts above.
- Compare with Optimize team's cost model spreadsheets (this doc intentionally smaller, per-profile).
- Hold weekly sync with quant-experiments on Tuesdays 11:00 starting next week.

Bottom line (working):
BitMix inspector aims to be the fast, explainable middle-layer between raw microbench outputs and customer-facing recommendations. This doc encodes a pragmatic cost/latency/quality tradeoff model and a set of draft heuristics; next step is to run the planned validation experiments and iterate the 'recommendation' thresholds based on real eval data.

-- Maya
